entries.81ec1427d0ff0c70a000a252b87b658695e18f19: <div sID="gen20046" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="3" osisID="Joel.3" sID="Joel.3"/> <div eID="gen20046" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20047" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen20048" type="x-p"/> In the close of the foregoing chapter we had a gracious promise of deliverance in Mount Zion and Jerusalem; now this whole chapter is a comment upon that promise, showing what that deliverance shall be, how it shall be wrought by the destruction of the church's enemies, and how it shall be perfected in the everlasting rest and joy of the church. This was in part accomplished in the deliverance of Jerusalem from the attempt that Sennacherib made upon it in Hezekiah's time, and afterwards in the return of the Jews out of their captivity in Babylon, and other deliverances wrought for the Jewish church between that and Christ's coming. But it has a further reference, to the great redemption wrought out for us by Jesus Christ, and the destruction of our spiritual enemies and all their agents, and will have its full accomplishment in the judgment of the great day. Here is a prediction, I. Of God's reckoning with the enemies of his people for all the injuries and indignities that they had done them, and returning them upon their own head, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.8">ver. 1-8</reference>. II. Of God's judging all nations when the measure of their iniquity is full, and appearing publicly, to the everlasting confusion of all impenitent sinners and the everlasting comfort of all his faithful servants, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.9-Joel.3.17">ver. 9-17</reference>. III. Of the provision God has made for the refreshment of his people, for their safety and purity, when their enemies shall be made desolate, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.18-Joel.3.21">ver. 18-21</reference>. These promises were not of private interpretation only, but were written for our learning, "that we, through patience and comfort of this scripture, might have hope."
entries.c8d24a7a79526fec1ff06a009318f5ad1e0af135: <div eID="gen20048" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen20047" type="introduction"/> <title type="x-s3">Threatenings against Israel's Enemies. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 720.)</title> <div sID="gen20049" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">1</hi> For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem, <hi type="super">2</hi> I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and <hi type="italic">for</hi> my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land. <hi type="super">3</hi> And they have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for a harlot, and sold a girl for wine, that they might drink. <hi type="super">4</hi> Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine? will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly <hi type="italic">and</hi> speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head; <hi type="super">5</hi> Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things: <hi type="super">6</hi> The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border. <hi type="super">7</hi> Behold, I will raise them out of the place whither ye have sold them, and will return your recompence upon your own head: <hi type="super">8</hi> And I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they shall sell them to the Sabeans, to a people far off: for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> hath spoken <hi type="italic">it.</hi> <div eID="gen20049" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20050" type="x-p"/> We have often heard of the <hi type="italic">year of the redeemed,</hi> and the <hi type="italic">year of recompences for the controversy of Zion;</hi> now here we have a description of the transactions of that year, and a prophecy of what shall be done when it comes, whenever it comes, for it comes often, and at the end of time it will come once for all. <div eID="gen20050" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20051" type="x-p"/> I. It shall be the <hi type="italic">year of the redeemed,</hi> for God will <hi type="italic">bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.1">v. 1</reference>. Though the bondage of God's people may be grievous and very long, yet it shall not be everlasting. That in Egypt ended at length in their deliverance into the glorious liberty of the children of God. <hi type="italic">Let my son go, the he may serve me.</hi> That in Babylon shall likewise end well. And the Lord Jesus will provide for the effectual redemption of poor enslaved souls from under the dominion of sin and Satan, and will proclaim that <hi type="italic">acceptable year,</hi> the year of jubilee, the release of debts and servants, and the <hi type="italic">opening of the prison to those that were bound.</hi> There is a day, there is a time, fixed for the <hi type="italic">bringing again of the captivity</hi> of God's children, for the redeeming of them <hi type="italic">from the power of the grave;</hi> and it shall be the <hi type="italic">last day</hi> and the end of all time. <div eID="gen20051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20052" type="x-p"/> II. It shall be the <hi type="italic">year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.</hi> Though God may suffer the enemies of his people to prevail against them very far and for a long time, yet he will call them to an account for it, and will lead captivity captive (<reference osisRef="Ps.68.18">Ps. lxviii. 18</reference>), will lead those captive that led his people captive, <reference osisRef="Rev.13.10">Rev. xiii. 10</reference>. Observe, <div eID="gen20052" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20053" type="x-p"/> 1. Who those are that shall be reckoned with—<hi type="italic">all nations,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">v. 2</reference>. This intimates, (1.) That all the nations had made themselves liable to the judgment of God for wrong done to his people. Persecution is the reigning crying sin of the world; that <hi type="italic">lying in wickedness</hi> itself is set against godliness. The enmity that is in the old serpent, <hi type="italic">the god of this world,</hi> against the seed of the woman, appears more or less in the <hi type="italic">children of this world. Marvel not if the world hate you.</hi> (2.) That, whatsoever nation injured God's nation, they should not go unpunished; for he that touches the Israel of God shall be made to know that he touches the apple of his eye. Jerusalem will be a <hi type="italic">burdensome stone to all people,</hi> <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">Zech. xii. 3</reference>. But the neighboring nations shall be particularly reckoned with—<hi type="italic">Tyre, and Sidon, and all the coasts of Palestine,</hi> or the Philistines, who have been troublesome neighbours to the Israel of God, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.4">v. 4</reference>. When the more remote and potent nations that laid Israel wastes are reckoned with the impotent malice of those that lay near them, and <hi type="italic">helped forward the affliction,</hi> (<reference osisRef="Zech.1.15">Zech. i. 15</reference>), and made a hand of it (<reference osisRef="Ezek.26.2">Ezek. xxvi. 2</reference>), shall not be passed by. Note, Little persecutors shall be called to an account as well as great ones; and, though they could not do much mischief, shall be reckoned with according to the <hi type="italic">wickedness of their endeavors</hi> and the mischief they would have done. <div eID="gen20053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20054" type="x-p"/> 2. The sitting of this court for judgment. They shall all be <hi type="italic">gathered</hi> (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">v. 2</reference>), that those who have combined together against God's people, <hi type="italic">with one consent</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.83.5">Ps. lxxxiii. 5</reference>), may together receive their doom. They shall be <hi type="italic">brought down into the valley of Jehoshaphat,</hi> which lay near Jerusalem, and there <hi type="italic">God will plead with them,</hi> (1.) Because it is fit that criminals should be tried in the same country where they did the fact. (2.) For their greater confusion, when they shall see that Jerusalem which they have so long endeavored and hoped for the ruin of, in spite of all their rage, made a <hi type="italic">praise in the earth.</hi> (3.) For the greater comfort and honor of God's Jerusalem, which shall see God pleading their cause. (4.) Then shall be re-acted what God did for Jehoshaphat when he gave him victory over those that invaded him, and furnished him and his people with matter of joy and praise, in the <hi type="italic">valley of Berachah.</hi> See <reference osisRef="2Chr.20.26">2 Chron. xx. 26</reference>. (5.) It was in this valley of Jehoshaphat (as Dr. Lightfoot suggests) that Sennacherib's army, or part of it, lay, when it was destroyed by an angel. They came together to ruin Jerusalem, but God brought them together for their own ruin, <hi type="italic">as sheaves into the floor,</hi> <reference osisRef="Mic.4.12">Mic. iv. 12</reference>. <div eID="gen20054" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20055" type="x-p"/> 3. The plaintiff called, on whose behalf this prosecution is set on foot; it is for <hi type="italic">my people,</hi> and <hi type="italic">for my heritage Israel.</hi> It is their cause that God will now plead with jealousy. Note, God's people are <hi type="italic">his heritage,</hi> his <hi type="italic">peculiar,</hi> his <hi type="italic">portion,</hi> his <hi type="italic">treasure,</hi> above all people, <reference osisRef="Exod.19.5">Exod. xix. 5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.32.9">Deut. xxxii. 9</reference>. They are his demesne, and therefore he has a good action against those that trespass upon them. <div eID="gen20055" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20056" type="x-p"/> 4. The charge exhibited against them, which is very particular. Many affronts they had put upon God by their idolatries, but that for which God has a quarrel with them is the affront they have put upon his people and upon the vessels of his sanctuary. <div eID="gen20056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20057" type="x-p"/> (1.) They had been very abusive to the people of Israel, had <hi type="italic">scattered them among the nations</hi> and forced them to seek for shelter where they could find a place, or carried them captive into their respective countries and there industriously dispersed them, for fear of their incorporating for their common safety. They <hi type="italic">parted their land,</hi> and took every one his share of it as their own; nay, they have <hi type="italic">cast lots for my people,</hi> and <hi type="italic">sold them.</hi> When they had taken them prisoners, [1.] They made a jest of them, made a scorn of them as of no value. They would not release them and yet thought them not worth the keeping; they made nothing of playing them away at dice. Or they made a dividend of the prisoners <hi type="italic">by lot,</hi> as the soldiers did of Christ's garments. [2.] They made a gain of them. When they had them they <hi type="italic">sold</hi> them, yet with so much contempt that they did <hi type="italic">not increase their wealth by their price,</hi> but sold them for their pleasure rather than their profit; they <hi type="italic">gave a boy</hi> taken in war for the <hi type="italic">hire of a harlot,</hi> and <hi type="italic">a girl</hi> for so many bottles of wine as would serve them for one sitting, a <hi type="italic">goodly price</hi> at which they valued them, and goodly preferment for a son and daughter of Israel to be a slave and a drudge in a tavern or a brothel. Observe, here, how that which is got by sin is commonly spent upon another. The spoil which these enemies of the Jews gathered by injustice and violence they scattered and threw away in drinking and whoring; such is frequently the character, and such the conversation, of the enemies and persecutors of the people of God. The Tyrians and Philistines, when they seized any of the children of Judah and Jerusalem, either took them prisoners in war or kidnapped them, they sold them to the Grecians (with whom the men of Tyre traded in the <hi type="italic">persons of men,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ezek.27.13">Ezek. xxvii. 13</reference>), that they <hi type="italic">might remove them far from their</hi> own <hi type="italic">border,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.6">v. 6</reference>. It was a great reproach to Israel, God's first-born, his free-born, to be thus bought and sold among the heathen. <div eID="gen20057" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20058" type="x-p"/> (2.) They had unjustly seized <hi type="italic">God's silver and gold</hi> (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.5">v. 5</reference>), by which some understand the wealth of Israel. The silver and gold which God's people had he calls his, because they had received it from him and devoted it to him; and whosoever robbed them God took it as if they had robbed him and would make reprisals accordingly. Those who take away the estates of good men for well-doing will be found guilty of sacrilege; they take God's <hi type="italic">silver and gold.</hi> But it seems rather to be meant of the <hi type="italic">vessels</hi> and <hi type="italic">treasures of the temple,</hi> which God here calls his <hi type="italic">goodly pleasant things,</hi> precious and desirable to him and all that are his. These they <hi type="italic">carried into their temples</hi> as trophies of their victory over God's Israel, thinking that therein they triumphed over Israel's God, nay, and that their idols triumphed over him. Thus the ark was put in Dagon's temple. Thus they did unjustly. "<hi type="italic">What have you to do with me</hi> (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.4">v. 4</reference>), with my people; what wrong have they done you? What provocation have they given you? You had nothing to do with them, and yet you do all this against them. Devices are devised against the <hi type="italic">quiet in the land,</hi> and those offended and harmed that are harmless and inoffensive: <hi type="italic">Will you render me a recompence?</hi>" Can they pretend that either God or his people have done them any injury, for which they may justify themselves by the law of retaliation in doing them these mischiefs? No; they have no colour for it. Note, It is no new thing for those who have been very civil and obliging to their neighbours to find them very unkind and unneighbourly and for those who do no injuries to suffer many. <div eID="gen20058" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20059" type="x-p"/> 5. The sentence passed upon them. In general (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.4">v. 4</reference>), "If <hi type="italic">you recompense me,</hi> if you pretend a quarrel with me, if you provoke me thus to jealousy, if you touch the apple of my eye, <hi type="italic">I will swiftly and speedily return your recompence upon your own head.</hi>" Those that contend with God will find themselves unable to make their part good with him. He will recompense them <hi type="italic">suddenly,</hi> when they little think of it, and have not time to prevent it; if he take them to task, he will soon effect their ruin. Particularly, it is threatened, (1.) That they should not gain their end in the mischief they designed against God's people. They thought to <hi type="italic">remove them so far from their border</hi> that they should never return to it again, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.6">v. 6</reference>. But (says God) "<hi type="italic">I will raise them out of the place whither you have sold them,</hi> and they shall not, as you intended, be buried alive there." Men's selling the people of God will not deprive him of his property in them. (2.) That they shall be paid in their own coin, as Adonibezek was (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.8">v. 8</reference>): "<hi type="italic">I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the children of Judah;</hi> you shall lie as much at their mercy as they have been at yours," <reference osisRef="Isa.60.14">Isa. lx. 14</reference>. Thus the Jews <hi type="italic">had rule over those that hated them,</hi> <reference osisRef="Esth.9.1">Esther ix. 1</reference>. And then they shall justly be <hi type="italic">sold to the Sabeans,</hi> to a <hi type="italic">people far off.</hi> This (some think) had its accomplishment in the victories obtained by the Maccabees over the enemies of the Jews; others think it looks as far forward as the last day, when the <hi type="italic">upright shall have dominion</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.49.14">Ps. xlix. 14</reference>) and <hi type="italic">the saints shall judge the world.</hi> It is certain that none ever hardened his heart against God, or his church, and prospered long; no, not Pharaoh himself, for <hi type="italic">the Lord has spoken it,</hi> for the comfort of all his suffering servants, that <hi type="italic">vengeance is his and he will repay.</hi>
entries.82e9c7c7d20d005d6e2dabb0b8eef4edc548363c: <div eID="gen20059" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Threatenings against Israel's Enemies. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 720.)</title> <div sID="gen20060" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">9</hi> Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men, let all the men of war draw near; let them come up: <hi type="super">10</hi> Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning-hooks into spears: let the weak say, I <hi type="italic">am</hi> strong. <hi type="super">11</hi> Assemble yourselves, and come, all ye heathen, and gather yourselves together round about: thither cause thy mighty ones to come down, <hi type="small-caps">O Lord</hi> . <hi type="super">12</hi> Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. <hi type="super">13</hi> Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness <hi type="italic">is</hi> great. <hi type="super">14</hi> Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> <hi type="italic">is</hi> near in the valley of decision. <hi type="super">15</hi> The sun and the moon shall be darkened, and the stars shall withdraw their shining. <hi type="super">16</hi> The <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> <hi type="italic">will be</hi> the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel. <hi type="super">17</hi> So shall ye know that I <hi type="italic">am</hi> the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> your God dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain: then shall Jerusalem be holy, and there shall no strangers pass through her any more. <div eID="gen20060" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20061" type="x-p"/> What the psalmist had long before ordered to be <hi type="italic">said among the heathen</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.96.10">Ps. xcvi. 10</reference>) the prophet here will have in like manner to be published to all nations, That <hi type="italic">the Lord reigns,</hi> and that <hi type="italic">he comes, he comes to judge the earth,</hi> as he had long been judging in the earth. The notice here given of God's judging the nations may have reference to the destruction of Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar, Antiochus, and to the Antichrist especially, and all the proud enemies of the Christian church; but some of the best interpreters, ancient and modern (particularly the learned Dr. Polock), think the scope of these verses is to set forth the day of the last judgment under the similitude of God's making war upon the enemies of his kingdom, and his gathering in the harvest of the earth, both which similitudes we find used in the Revelation, <reference osisRef="Rev.19.11">ch. xix. 11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.14.18">xiv. 18</reference>. Here we have, <div eID="gen20061" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20062" type="x-p"/> I. A challenge given to all the enemies of God's kingdom to do their worst. To signify to them that God is preparing war against them, they are called upon to prepare war against him, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.9-Joel.3.11">v. 9-11</reference>. When the hour of God's judgment shall come effectual methods shall be taken to gather all nations <hi type="italic">to the battle of that great day of God Almighty,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.16.14">Rev. xvi. 14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.20.8">xx. 8</reference>. It seems to be here spoken ironically: "<hi type="italic">Proclaim you this among the Gentiles;</hi> let all the forces of the nations be summoned to join in confederacy against God and his people." It is like that, <reference osisRef="Isa.7.9">Isa. vii. 9</reference>, "<hi type="italic">Associate yourselves, O you people!</hi> and <hi type="italic">gird yourselves,</hi> but you shall be <hi type="italic">broken to pieces.</hi> <hi type="italic">Prepare war;</hi> muster up all your strength; <hi type="italic">wake up the mighty men;</hi> call them into your service; excite them to vigilance and resolution; <hi type="italic">let all the men of war draw near. Let them come</hi> and enter the lists with Omnipotence if they dare; let them not complain for want of weapons, but let them <hi type="italic">beat their ploughshares into swords</hi> and their <hi type="italic">pruning-hooks into spears.</hi> Let them resolve, if they will, never to return to their husbandry again, but either to conquer or die; let none plead unfitness to bear arms, but <hi type="italic">let the weak say, I am strong</hi> and will venture into the field of battle." Thus does a God of almighty power bid defiance to all the opposition of the powers of darkness; let the <hi type="italic">heathen rage,</hi> and the <hi type="italic">kings of the earth take counsel together, against the Lord and his Christ;</hi> let them <hi type="italic">assemble, and come,</hi> and <hi type="italic">gather themselves together;</hi> but he that sits in heaven shall laugh at them, and, while he thus calls them, he has them in derision, <reference osisRef="Ps.2.1">Ps. ii. 1</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.2.4">4</reference>. The heathen must be wakened, must be raised from the dead, that they may <hi type="italic">come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat,</hi> to receive their doom (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.12">v. 12</reference>), may come up out of their graves, come up <hi type="italic">into the air,</hi> to meet the Lord there. Jehoshaphat signifies <hi type="italic">the judgment of the Lord.</hi> Let them come to the place of God's judgment, which perhaps is the chief reason for the using of this name here, but it is put together as a proper name for the sake of allusions to the place so called, which we observed before; let them come thither where God will <hi type="italic">sit to judge the heathen,</hi> to that <hi type="italic">throne of glory</hi> before which shall be <hi type="italic">gathered all nations</hi> (<reference osisRef="Matt.25.32">Matt. xxv. 32</reference>), for before the judgment-seat of Christ <hi type="italic">we must all appear.</hi> The challenge (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9">v. 9</reference>) is turned into a summons, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.12">v. 12</reference>. It is not only, <hi type="italic">Come if you dare,</hi> but <hi type="italic">You shall come</hi> whether you will or no, for there is no escaping the judgments of God. <div eID="gen20062" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20063" type="x-p"/> II. A charge given to the ministers of God's justice to appear and act against these daring enemies of his kingdom among men: And therefore <hi type="italic">cause thy mighty ones to come down, O Lord!</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.11">v. 11</reference>. When they bring their forces into the field, let God bring his, let the archangel's trumpet sound a charge, to call together his <hi type="italic">mighty ones,</hi> that is, his angels. Perhaps it is with reference to this that Christ's coming from heaven at the last day is said to be <hi type="italic">with his mighty angels,</hi> <reference osisRef="2Thess.1.7">2 Thess. i. 7</reference>. These are the <hi type="italic">hosts of the Lord,</hi> that shall fight his battles when he shall put down all opposing rule, principality, and power when he shall <hi type="italic">judge among the heathen,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.110.6">Ps. cx. 6</reference>. Some think these words (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9-Joel.3.10">v. 9, 10</reference>), <hi type="italic">Prepare war, wake up the mighty men,</hi> are not a challenge to the enemies' hosts, but a charge to God's hosts; let them <hi type="italic">draw near, and come up.</hi> When God's cause is to be pleaded, either by the law or by the sword, he has those ready that shall please it effectually, witnesses ready to appear for him in the court of judgment, soldiers ready to appear for him in the field of battle. They shall <hi type="italic">beat ploughshares into swords,</hi> if need be. However, it is plain that to them the charge in given (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.13">v. 13</reference>), <hi type="italic">Put you in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe;</hi> that is, <hi type="italic">their wickedness is great,</hi> the measure of it is full, and they are ripe for ruin. Our Saviour has expounded this, <reference osisRef="Matt.13.39">Matt. xiii. 39</reference>. <hi type="italic">The harvest is the end of the world, and the reapers are the angels.</hi> And they are commanded to <hi type="italic">thrust</hi> in their <hi type="italic">sickle. their sharp sickle,</hi> and gather in both the <hi type="italic">harvest</hi> and the <hi type="italic">vintage,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.14.15">Rev. xiv. 15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rev.14.18">18</reference>. Note, The greatness of men's wickedness makes them ripe for God's judgment. <div eID="gen20063" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20064" type="x-p"/> III. The vast appearance that shall be in that great and solemn day (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.14">v. 14</reference>): <hi type="italic">Multitudes, multitudes, in the valley of decision,</hi> the same which before was called the <hi type="italic">valley of Jehoshaphat,</hi> or <hi type="italic">of the judgment of the Lord,</hi> for the <hi type="italic">day of the Lord is near</hi> in that valley. Note, 1. The judgment-day, that day of the Lord, has all along been looked upon, and spoken of, as <hi type="italic">nigh at hand.</hi> Enoch said, <hi type="italic">Behold, the Lord comes,</hi> as if the Judge were then standing before the do or, because it is certain that that day will come and will come according to the appointment, and a <hi type="italic">thousand years with God are but as one day;</hi> things are ripening apace for it; we ought always to be ready for it, because our judgment is at hand. 2. The day of judgment will be the <hi type="italic">day of decision,</hi> when every man's eternal state will be determined, and the controversy that has been long depending between the kingdom of Christ and that of Satan shall be finally decided, and an end put to the struggle. <hi type="italic">The valley of the distribution of judgment</hi> (so the Chaldee), when <hi type="italic">every man shall receive according to the things done in the body. The valley of threshing</hi> (so the margin), carrying on the metaphor of the <hi type="italic">harvest,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.13">v. 13</reference>. The proud enemies of God's people will then be crushed and broken to pieces, and made as the <hi type="italic">dust of the summer threshing-floors.</hi> 3. Innumerable multitudes will be gathered together to receive their final doom in that day, as in the destruction of Gog we read of the valley of <hi type="italic">Hamon-Gog,</hi> and the city of <hi type="italic">Hamonah</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.39.15-Ezek.39.16">Ezek. xxxix. 15, 16</reference>), both signifying the <hi type="italic">multitude</hi> of the vanquished enemies; it is the word here used, <hi type="italic">Hamonim, Hamonim,</hi> expressed by the way of admiration—O what vast multitudes of sinners will divine justice be glorified in the ruin of at that day! <hi type="italic">A multitude of living</hi> (says one of the rabbin) <hi type="italic">and a multitude of dead,</hi> for Christ shall come <hi type="italic">to judge both the quick and the dead.</hi> <div eID="gen20064" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20065" type="x-p"/> IV. The amazing change that shall then be made in the kingdom of nature (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.15">v. 15</reference>): <hi type="italic">The sun and moon shall be darkened,</hi> as before, <reference osisRef="Joel.2.31">ch. ii. 31</reference>. Their glory and lustre shall be eclipsed by the far greater brightness of that glory in which the Judge shall then appear. Nay, they shall themselves be set aside in the dissolution of all things; for the damned sinners in hell shall not be allowed their light, for God himself will be <hi type="italic">their everlasting light,</hi> <reference osisRef="Isa.60.19">Isa. lx. 19</reference>. Those that fall under the wrath of God in that day of wrath shall be cut off from all comfort and joy, signified by the darkening not only of sun and moon, but of the stars also. <div eID="gen20065" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20066" type="x-p"/> V. The different impressions which that day will make upon the children of this world and the children of God, according as it will be to them. 1. To the wicked it will be a terrible day. <hi type="italic">The Lord</hi> shall then speak <hi type="italic">from Zion and Jerusalem,</hi> from the throne of his glory, from heaven, where he manifests himself in a peculiar manner, as sometimes he has done in the <hi type="italic">glorious high throne of his sanctuary,</hi> which yet was but a faint resemblance of the glory of that day. He shall speak <hi type="italic">from heaven,</hi> from <hi type="italic">the midst</hi> of his saints and angels (so some understand it), the holy society of which may be called <hi type="italic">Zion</hi> and <hi type="italic">Jerusalem;</hi> for, when we come to the <hi type="italic">heavenly Jerusalem,</hi> we come to the <hi type="italic">innumerable company of angels;</hi> see <reference osisRef="Heb.12.22">Heb. xii. 22, 25</reference>. Now is speaking in that day will be to the wicked as <hi type="italic">roaring,</hi> terrible as the roaring of a lion (for so the word signifies); he long kept silence, but now <hi type="italic">our God shall come, and shall not keep silence,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.50.3">Ps. l. 3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.50.21">21</reference>. Note, The judgment of the great day will make the ears of those to tingle that continue the implacable enemies of God's kingdom. God's voice will then <hi type="italic">shake terribly</hi> both <hi type="italic">heaven and earth</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.21">Isa. ii. 21</reference>), yet <hi type="italic">once more,</hi> <reference osisRef="Hag.2.6">Hag. ii. 6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Heb.12.26">Heb. xii. 26</reference>. This denotes that the voice of God will in the great day speak such terror to the wicked as were enough to put even heaven and earth into a consternation. When God comes to pull down and destroy his enemies, and make them all his footstool, though heaven and earth should stand up in defence of them and undertake their protection, it shall be all in vain. Even they shall shake before him and be an insufficient shelter to those whom he comforts forth to contend with. Note, As blessings out of Zion are the sweetest blessings, and enough to make heaven and earth sing, so terrors out of Zion are the sorest terrors, and enough to make heaven and earth shake. 2. To the righteous it will be a joyful day. When the heaven and earth shall tremble, and be dissolved and burnt up, then will the Lord be the <hi type="italic">hope of his people</hi> and the <hi type="italic">strength of the children of Israel</hi> (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.16">v. 16</reference>), and <hi type="italic">then shall Jerusalem be holy,</hi> <reference osisRef="Joel.3.17">v. 17</reference>. The saints are the Israel of God; they are <hi type="italic">his people;</hi> the church is his Jerusalem. They are in covenant and communion with him; now in the great day, (1.) Their longings shall be satisfied: <hi type="italic">The Lord will be the hope of his people.</hi> As he always was the founder and foundation of their hopes, so he then will be the crown of their hopes. He will be the <hi type="italic">harbour</hi> of his people (so the word is), their receptacle, refuge, and home. The saints in the great day shall arrive at the desired haven, shall put to shore after a stormy voyage; they shall go to be for ever at home with God, to their Father's house, the house <hi type="italic">not made with hands.</hi> (2.) Their happiness shall be confirmed. God will be in that day the <hi type="italic">strength of the children of Israel,</hi> enabling them to bid that day welcome and to bear up under the weight of its glories and joys. In this world, when the judgments of God are abroad, and sinners are falling under them, God is and will be the hope and strength of his people, the strength of their heart, and their portion, when other men's hearts fail them for fear. (3.) Their holiness shall be completed (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.17">v. 17</reference>): <hi type="italic">Then shall Jerusalem be holy,</hi> the <hi type="italic">holy city</hi> indeed; such shall the heavenly Jerusalem be, such the glorious church, <hi type="italic">without spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing. Jerusalem shall be holiness</hi> (so the word is); it shall be perfectly holy; there shall be no remainder of sin in it. The gospel-church is a holy society, even in its militant state, but will never be holiness itself till it comes to be triumphant. Then <hi type="italic">no stranger shall pass through her any more;</hi> there shall not enter into the New Jerusalem any thing that defiles or works iniquity; none shall be there but those who have a right to be there, none but its own citizens; for it shall be an unmixed society. (4.) God shall in all this be manifested and magnified: <hi type="italic">So shall you know that I am the Lord your God.</hi> By the sanctifying and glorifying of the church God will be known in his holiness and glory, as the God that dwells in his holy mountain and makes it holy by dwelling in it; and those that are sanctified and glorified are so <hi type="italic">through the knowledge of him</hi> that called them. The knowledge which true believers have of God is, [1.] An appropriating knowledge. They know that he is <hi type="italic">the Lord their God,</hi> yet not theirs only, but theirs in common with the whole church, that he is their God, but <hi type="italic">dwelling in Zion his holy mountain;</hi> for, though faith appropriates, it does not engross or monopolize the privileges of the covenant. [2.] It is an experimental knowledge. They shall find him their <hi type="italic">hope and strength</hi> in the worst of times, and so they shall <hi type="italic">know that he is the Lord their God.</hi> Those know best the goodness of God who have tasted and seen it, and have found him good to them.
entries.cea08fbae3c98b8f9fb277d1518dd8cf2642f7dd: <div eID="gen20066" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3">Judgments and Mercies; Promises to the Church. (<hi type="small-caps">b. c.</hi> 720.)</title> <div sID="gen20067" type="x-p"/> <hi type="super">18</hi> And it shall come to pass in that day, <hi type="italic">that</hi> the mountains shall drop down new wine, and the hills shall flow with milk, and all the rivers of Judah shall flow with waters, and a fountain shall come forth of the house of the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> , and shall water the valley of Shittim. <hi type="super">19</hi> Egypt shall be a desolation, and Edom shall be a desolate wilderness, for the violence <hi type="italic">against</hi> the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land. <hi type="super">20</hi> But Judah shall dwell for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation. <hi type="super">21</hi> For I will cleanse their blood <hi type="italic">that</hi> I have not cleansed: for the <hi type="small-caps">Lord</hi> dwelleth in Zion. <div eID="gen20067" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20068" type="x-p"/> These promises with which this prophecy concludes have their accomplishments in part in the kingdom of grace, and the comforts and graces of all the faithful subjects of that kingdom, but will have their full accomplishment in the kingdom of glory; for, as to the Jewish church, we know not of any event concerning that which answers to the extent of these promises, and what instances of peace and prosperity they were blessed with, which they may be supposed to be a hyperbolical description of, they were but figures of <hi type="italic">better things</hi> reserved <hi type="italic">for us, that they</hi> in their best estate <hi type="italic">without us might not be made perfect.</hi> <div eID="gen20068" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20069" type="x-p"/> I. It is promised that the enemies of the church shall be vanquished and brought down, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.19">v. 19</reference>. Egypt, that old enemy of Israel, and Edom, which had an inveterate enmity to Israel, derived from Esau, these <hi type="italic">shall be a desolation,</hi> a <hi type="italic">desolate wilderness,</hi> no more to be inhabited; they have become the <hi type="italic">people of God's curse;</hi> so the Idumeans were, <reference osisRef="Isa.34.5">Isa. xxxiv. 5</reference>. No strength nor wealth of a nation is a defence against the judgment of God. But what is the quarrel God has with these potent kingdoms? It is for their <hi type="italic">violence against the children of Judah,</hi> and the injuries they had done them; see <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.3 Ezek.25.8 Ezek.25.12 Ezek.25.15">Ezek. xxv. 3, 8, 12, 15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.26.2">xxvi. 2</reference>. They had <hi type="italic">shed</hi> the <hi type="italic">innocent blood</hi> of the Jews that fled to them for shelter or were making their escape through their country. Note, The innocent blood of God's people is very precious to him, and not a drop of it shall be shed but it shall be reckoned for. In the last day this earth, which has been filled with violence against the people of God, shall be made a desolation, when it and all the works that are therein shall be burnt up. And, sooner or later, the oppressors and persecutors of God's Israel shall be brought down and laid in the dust, nay, they will at length be brought down and laid in the flames. <div eID="gen20069" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20070" type="x-p"/> II. It is promised that the church shall be very happy; and truly happy it is in spiritual privileges, even during its militant state, but much more when it comes to be triumphant. Three things are here promised it:— <div eID="gen20070" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20071" type="x-p"/> 1. Purity. This is put last here, as a reason for the rest (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.21">v. 21</reference>); but we may consider it first, as the ground and foundation of the rest: <hi type="italic">I will cleanse their blood that I have not cleansed,</hi> that is, their bloody heinous sins, especially shedding innocent blood; that filth and guilt they had contracted by sin, which rendered them unfit for communion with God, and made them odious to his holiness and obnoxious to his justice; this they shall be washed from in the <hi type="italic">fountain opened,</hi> <reference osisRef="Zech.13.1">Zech. xiii. 1</reference>. That shall be cleansed by the blood of Christ which could not be cleansed by the sacrifices and purifications of the ceremonial law. Or, if we apply it to the happiness of a future state, it intimates the cleansing of the saints from all these corruptions from which they were not cleansed either by ordinances or providences in the world; there shall not be the least remains of sin in them there. Here, though they are washing daily, there is still something that is not cleansed; but in heaven, even that also shall be done away. And the reason is because <hi type="italic">the Lord dwells in Zion,</hi> dwells with his church, and much more gloriously with that in heaven, and <hi type="italic">holiness becomes his house for ever,</hi> for which reason, where he dwells there must be, there shall be, a perfection of holiness. Note, Though the refining and reforming of the church is work that goes on slowly, and still there is something we complain of that is <hi type="italic">not cleansed,</hi> yet there is a day coming when every thing that is amiss shall be amended, and the church shall be all fair, and no spot, no stain in her; and we must wait for that day. <div eID="gen20071" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20072" type="x-p"/> 2. Plenty, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.18">v. 18</reference>. This is put first, because it is the reverse of the judgment threatened in the foregoing chapters. (1.) The streams of this plenty overflow the land and enrich it: <hi type="italic">The mountains shall drop new wine</hi> and <hi type="italic">the hills shall flow with milk,</hi> such great abundance shall they have of suitable provision, both for <hi type="italic">babes</hi> and for <hi type="italic">strong men.</hi> It intimates the abundance of vineyards, and all fruitful; and the abundance of cattle in the pastures that fill them with milk. And, to make the corn-land fruitful, the <hi type="italic">rivers of Judah shall flow with water,</hi> so that the country shall be like the garden of Eden, well-watered every where and greatly enriched, <reference osisRef="Ps.65.9">Ps. lxv. 9</reference>. But this seems to be meant spiritually; the graces and comforts of the new covenant are compared to <hi type="italic">wine and milk</hi> (<reference osisRef="Isa.55.1">Isa. lv. 1</reference>), and the Spirit to <hi type="italic">rivers of living water,</hi> <reference osisRef="John.7.38">John vii. 38</reference>. And these gifts abound much more under the New Testament than they did under the Old; when believers receive <hi type="italic">grace for grace</hi> from Christ's fulness, when they are enriched with <hi type="italic">everlasting consolations,</hi> and <hi type="italic">filled with joy and peace in believing,</hi> then <hi type="italic">the mountains drop new wine,</hi> and <hi type="italic">the hills flow with milk. Drink you,</hi> drink abundantly, <hi type="italic">O beloved!</hi> When there is plentiful effusion of the Spirit of grace, then the <hi type="italic">rivers of Judah flow with water,</hi> and make glad, not only <hi type="italic">the city of our God</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ps.46.4">Ps. xlvi. 4</reference>), but the whole land. (2.) The fountain of this plenty is in the <hi type="italic">house of God,</hi> whence the streams take their rise, as those <hi type="italic">waters of the sanctuary</hi> (<reference osisRef="Ezek.47.1">Ezek. xlvii. 1</reference>) from <hi type="italic">under the threshold of the house,</hi> and the river of life <hi type="italic">out of the throne of God and the Lamb,</hi> <reference osisRef="Rev.22.1">Rev. xxii. 1</reference>. The psalmist, speaking of Zion, says, <hi type="italic">All my springs are in thee,</hi> <reference osisRef="Ps.87.7">Ps. lxxxvii. 7</reference>. Those that take temporal blessings to be meant in the former part of the verse, yet by this <hi type="italic">fountain</hi> out of <hi type="italic">the house of the Lord</hi> understand the grace of God, which, if we abound in temporal blessings, we have so much more need of, that we may not abuse them. Christ himself is the fountain; his merit and grace cleanse us, refresh us, and make us fruitful. This is said to water <hi type="italic">the valley of Shittim,</hi> which lay a great way off from the temple at Jerusalem, on the other side of Jordan, and was a dry and barren valley, which intimates that gospel-grace, flowing from Christ, shall reach far, even to the Gentile world, to the most remote regions of it, and shall make those to abound in the fruits of righteousness who had long lain as the barren wilderness. This grace is a fountain overflowing, ever-flowing, from which we may be continually drawing, and yet need not fear its being drawn dry. This fountain comes <hi type="italic">out of the house of the Lord</hi> above, from his temple in heaven, flows all that good which here we are daily tasting the streams of, but hope to be shortly, hope to be eternally, drinking at the fountain-head of. <div eID="gen20072" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20073" type="x-p"/> 3. Perpetuity. This crowns all the rest (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.20">v. 20</reference>): <hi type="italic">Judah shall dwell for ever</hi> (when Egypt and Edom are made <hi type="italic">a desolation</hi>), and Jerusalem shall continue <hi type="italic">from generation to generation.</hi> This is a promise, and a precious promise it is, (1.) That the church of Christ shall continue in the world to the end of time. As one generation of professing Christians passes away, another shall come, in whom the <hi type="italic">throne</hi> of Christ <hi type="italic">shall endure for ever,</hi> and <hi type="italic">the gates of hell shall not prevail</hi> against it. (2.) That all the living members of that church (Judah and Jerusalem are put for the <hi type="italic">inhabitants</hi> of that city and country, <reference osisRef="Matt.3.5">Matt. iii. 5</reference>) shall be established in their happiness to the utmost ages of eternity. This new Jerusalem shall be <hi type="italic">from generation to generation,</hi> for it is a city that has foundations, not made with hands, but eternal in the heavens.  <chapter eID="Joel.3"/> <div eID="gen20073" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen19991" osisID="Joel" type="book"/>

entries.b1b82b1957a58b303357cc2aab9e3c8edc50f315: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12486"/><title type="x-s2">CHAPTER 3</title> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.21">Joe 3:1-21</reference>. God's Vengeance on Israel's Foes in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. His Blessing on the Church.</title> <div sID="gen22950" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12486"/><hi type="bold">1. bring again the captivity--</hi>that is, reverse it. The Jews restrict this to the return from Babylon. Christians refer it to the coming of Christ. But the prophet comprises the whole redemption, beginning from the return out of Babylon, then continued from the first advent of Christ down to the last day (His second advent), when God will restore His Church to perfect felicity [Calvin]. <div eID="gen22950" type="x-p"/>
entries.cf6df42937c08d8e2fccb48f62b55569ac1642d4: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12487"/><div sID="gen22951" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12487"/>2. Parallel to <reference osisRef="Zech.14.2">Zec 14:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zech.3.4">3, 4</reference>, where the "Mount of Olives" answers to the "Valley of Jehoshaphat" here. The latter is called "the valley of blessing" (Berachah) (<reference osisRef="2Chr.20.26">2Ch 20:26</reference>). It lies between Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives and has the Kedron flowing through it. As Jehoshaphat overthrew the confederate foes of Judah, namely, Ammon, Moab, &c. (<reference osisRef="Ps.83.6-Ps.83.8">Psa 83:6-8</reference>), in this valley, so God was to overthrow the Tyrians, Zidonians, Philistines, Edom, and Egypt, with a similar utter overthrow (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.4">Joe 3:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Joel.3.19">19</reference>). This has been long ago fulfilled; but the ultimate event shadowed forth herein is still future, when God shall specially interpose to destroy Jerusalem's last foes, of whom Tyre, Zidon, Edom, Egypt, and Philistia are the types. As "Jehoshaphat" means "the judgment of Jehovah," the valley of Jehoshaphat may be used as a general term for the theater of God's final judgments on Israel's foes, with an allusion to the judgment inflicted on them by Jehoshaphat. The definite mention of the Mount of Olives in <reference osisRef="Zech.14.4">Zec 14:4</reference>, and the fact that this was the scene of the ascension, makes it likely the same shall be the scene of Christ's coming again: compare "this same Jesus ... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen Him go into heaven" (<reference osisRef="Acts.1.11">Ac 1:11</reference>).<div eID="gen22951" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22952" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">all nations--</hi>namely, which have maltreated Judah.<div eID="gen22952" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22953" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">plead with them--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.66.16">Is 66:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.22">Eze 38:22</reference>).<div eID="gen22953" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22954" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my heritage Israel--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Deut.32.9">De 32:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.10.16">Jr 10:16</reference>). Implying that the source of Judah's redemption is God's free love, wherewith He chose Israel as His peculiar heritage, and at the same time assuring them, when desponding because of trials, that He would plead their cause as His own, and as if He were injured in their person. <div eID="gen22954" type="x-p"/>
entries.ecd3e01a8b97ceb403889a981679d24c6ab0b577: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12488"/><div sID="gen22955" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12488"/><hi type="bold">3. cast lots for my people--</hi>that is, divided among themselves My people as their captives by lot. Compare as to the distribution of captives by lot (Ob 11; <reference osisRef="Nah.3.10">Na 3:10</reference>).<div eID="gen22955" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22956" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">given a boy for ... harlot--</hi>Instead of paying a harlot for her prostitution in money, they gave her a Jewish captive boy as a slave.<div eID="gen22956" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22957" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">girl for wine--</hi>So valueless did they regard a Jewish girl that they would sell her for a draught of wine. <div eID="gen22957" type="x-p"/>
entries.0e7fb50da2170e77ef3b6d10e0249db9c72484a8: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12489"/><div sID="gen22958" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12489"/><hi type="bold">4. what have ye to do with me--</hi>Ye have no connection with Me (that is, with My people: God identifying Himself with Israel); I (that is, My people) have given you no cause of quarrel, why then do ye trouble Me (that is, My people)? (Compare the same phrase, <reference osisRef="Josh.22.24">Jos 22:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="Judg.11.12">Jud 11:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Sam.16.10">2Sa 16:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.8.29">Mt 8:29</reference>).<div eID="gen22958" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22959" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Tyre ... Zidon ... Palestine--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Amos.1.6">Am 1:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.9">9</reference>).<div eID="gen22959" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22960" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">if ye recompense me--</hi>If ye injure Me (My people), in revenge for fancied wrongs (<reference osisRef="Ezek.25.15-Ezek.25.17">Eze 25:15-17</reference>), I will requite you in your own coin swiftly and speedily. <div eID="gen22960" type="x-p"/>
entries.3dac944c07464b5ef3619ec30212bef6d0843a0b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12490"/><div sID="gen22961" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12490"/><hi type="bold">5. my silver ... my gold--</hi>that is, the gold and silver of My people. The Philistines and Arabians had carried off all the treasures of King Jehoram's house (<reference osisRef="2Chr.21.16">2Ch 21:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="2Chr.21.17">17</reference>). Compare also <reference osisRef="1Kgs.15.18">1Ki 15:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.12.18">2Ki 12:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="2Kgs.14.14">14:14</reference>, for the spoiling of the treasures of the temple and the king's palace in Judah by Syria. It was customary among the heathen to hang up in the idol temples some of the spoils of war as presents to their gods. <div eID="gen22961" type="x-p"/>
entries.33808da5412670c6b678847ca1f053851731859c: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12491"/><div sID="gen22962" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12491"/><hi type="bold">6. Grecians--</hi>literally, "Javanites," that is, the Ionians, a Greek colony on the coast of Asia Minor who were the first Greeks known to the Jews. The Greeks themselves, however, in their original descent came from Javan (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.2">Ge 10:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.4">4</reference>). Probably the germ of Greek civilization in part came through the Jewish slaves imported into Greece from Phoenicia by traffickers. <reference osisRef="Ezek.27.13">Eze 27:13</reference> mentions Javan and Tyre as trading in the persons of men.<div eID="gen22962" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22963" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">far from their border--</hi>far from Judea; so that the captive Jews were cut off from all hope of return. <div eID="gen22963" type="x-p"/>
entries.6155d7a5e4cd544859a1ab80b56d75834a6058a5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12492"/><div sID="gen22964" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12492"/><hi type="bold">7. raise them--</hi>that is, I will rouse them. Neither sea nor distance will prevent My bringing them back. Alexander, and his successors, restored to liberty many Jews in bondage in Greece [Josephus, Antiquities, 13.5; Wars of the Jews, 3.9,2]. <div eID="gen22964" type="x-p"/>
entries.65187bf67ae882c9d7bfadc6bc530af5a25699c9: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12493"/><div sID="gen22965" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12493"/><hi type="bold">8. sell them to ... Sabeans--</hi>The Persian Artaxerxes Mnemon and Darius Ochus, and chiefly the Greek Alexander, reduced the Phoenician and Philistine powers. Thirty thousand Tyrians after the capture of Tyre by the last conqueror, and multitudes of Philistines on the taking of Gaza, were sold as slaves. The Jews are here said to do that which the God of Judah does in vindication of their wrong, namely, sell the Phoenicians who sold them, to a people "far off," as was Greece, whither the Jews had been sold. The Sabeans at the most remote extremity of Arabia Felix are referred to (compare <reference osisRef="Jer.6.20">Jr 6:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.12.42">Mt 12:42</reference>). <div eID="gen22965" type="x-p"/>
entries.19b65ee3c42d00761e3e8b59c1305b3f530f4224: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12494"/><div sID="gen22966" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12494"/>9. The nations hostile to Israel are summoned by Jehovah to "come up" (this phrase is used because Jerusalem was on a hill) against Jerusalem, not that they may destroy it, but to be destroyed by the Lord (<reference osisRef="Ezek.38.7-Ezek.38.23">Eze 38:7-23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.2-Zech.9.14">Zec 12:2-9; 14</reference>:2, 3).<div eID="gen22966" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22967" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Prepare war--</hi>literally, sanctify war: because the heathen always began war with religious ceremonies. The very phrase used of Babylon's preparations against Jerusalem (<reference osisRef="Jer.6.4">Jr 6:4</reference>) is now used of the final foes of Jerusalem. As Babylon was then desired by God to advance against her for her destruction, so now all her foes, of whom Babylon was the type, are desired to advance against her for their own destruction. <div eID="gen22967" type="x-p"/>
entries.7bdb54736e73f2f8be08ffe36954df22d2af9ee2: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12495"/><div sID="gen22968" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12495"/><hi type="bold">10. Beat your ploughshares into swords--</hi>As the foes are desired to "beat their ploughshares into swords, and their pruning hooks into spears," that so they may perish in their unhallowed attack on Judah and Jerusalem, so these latter, and the nations converted to God by them, after the overthrow of the antichristian confederacy, shall, on the contrary, "beat their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into pruning hooks," when under Messiah's coming reign there shall be war no more (<reference osisRef="Isa.2.4">Is 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.18">Ho 2:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.3">Mi 4:3</reference>).<div eID="gen22968" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22969" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">let the weak say, I am strong--</hi>So universal shall be the rage of Israel's foes for invading her, that even the weak among them will fancy themselves strong enough to join the invading forces. Age and infirmity were ordinarily made valid excuses for exemption from service, but so mad shall be the fury of the world against God's people, that even the feeble will not desire to be exempted (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.2.1-Ps.2.3">Psa 2:1-3</reference>). <div eID="gen22969" type="x-p"/>
entries.504ad2c92d25f68fff2a3f30f5d225e9d574bbac: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12496"/><div sID="gen22970" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12496"/><hi type="bold">11. Assemble--</hi>"Hasten" [Maurer].<div eID="gen22970" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22971" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thither--</hi>to the valley of Jehoshaphat.<div eID="gen22971" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22972" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">thy mighty ones--</hi>the warriors who fancy themselves "mighty ones," but who are on that very spot to be overthrown by Jehovah [Maurer]. Compare "the mighty men" (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9">Joe 3:9</reference>). Rather, Joel speaks of God's really "mighty ones" in contrast to the self-styled "mighty men" (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.9">Joe 3:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.103.20">Psa 103:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.13.3">Is 13:3</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Dan.10.13">Da 10:13</reference>). Auberlen remarks: One prophet supplements the other, for they all prophesied only "in part." What was obscure to one was revealed to the other; what is briefly described by one is more fully so by another. Daniel calls Antichrist a king, and dwells on his worldly conquests; John looks more to his spiritual tyranny, for which reason he adds a second beast, wearing the semblance of spirituality. Antichrist himself is described by Daniel. Isaiah (<reference osisRef="Isa.29.1-Isa.29.24">Is 29:1-24</reference>), Joel (<reference osisRef="Joel.3.1-Joel.3.21">Joe 3:1-21</reference>) and Zechariah (Zec 12:<reference osisRef="1Cor.14.21">1-14:21</reference>), describe his army of heathen followers coming up against Jerusalem, but not Antichrist himself. <div eID="gen22972" type="x-p"/>
entries.a27800ca2da5fc86bd70477dfe431dbee21076cb: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12497"/><div sID="gen22973" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12497"/>12. See <reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>.<div eID="gen22973" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22974" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">judge all the heathen round about--</hi>that is, all the nations from all parts of the earth which have maltreated Israel; not merely, as Henderson supposes, the nations round about Jerusalem (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.110.6">Psa 110:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.2.4">Is 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.3">Mi 4:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.11-Mic.4.13">11-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.15-Zeph.3.19">Zep 3:15-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.9">Zec 12:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.3-Zech.14.11">14:3-11</reference>; Mal 4:1-3). <div eID="gen22974" type="x-p"/>
entries.9b0c699277b1939545c0234a4f1db63edf5a4dca: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12498"/><div sID="gen22975" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12498"/>13. Direction to the ministers of vengeance to execute God's wrath, as the enemy's wickedness is come to its full maturity. God does not cut off the wicked at once, but waits till their guilt is at its full (so as to the Amorites' iniquity, <reference osisRef="Gen.15.16">Ge 15:16</reference>), to show forth His own long-suffering, and the justice of their doom who have so long abused it (Mt 13:27-30, 38, 40; <reference osisRef="Rev.14.15-Rev.14.19">Re 14:15-19</reference>). For the image of a harvest to be threshed, compare <reference osisRef="Jer.51.33">Jr 51:33</reference>; and a wine-press, <reference osisRef="Isa.63.3">Is 63:3</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lam.1.15">La 1:15</reference>. <div eID="gen22975" type="x-p"/>
entries.410c817542caa9d7f01e8da7e2cb4eff6ed082cb: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12499"/><div sID="gen22976" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12499"/>14. The prophet in vision seeing the immense array of nations congregating, exclaims, "Multitudes, multitudes!" a Hebraism for immense multitudes.<div eID="gen22976" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22977" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">valley of decision--</hi>that is, the valley in which they are to meet their "determined doom." The same as "the valley of Jehoshaphat," that is, "the valley of judgment" (see on <reference osisRef="Joel.3.2">Joe 3:2</reference>). Compare <reference osisRef="Joel.3.12">Joe 3:12</reference>, "there will I sit to judge," which confirms English Version rather than Margin, "threshing." The repetition of "valley of decision" heightens the effect and pronounces the awful certainty of their doom. <div eID="gen22977" type="x-p"/>
entries.70bc2f5aa8eb7bd2e9832b68050d4a8b88e470b3: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12500"/><div sID="gen22978" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12500"/>15. (See on <reference osisRef="Joel.2.10">Joe 2:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.2.30">Joe 2:30</reference>). <div eID="gen22978" type="x-p"/>
entries.f516ca20a12217d9d0f9ce1daf9aead201c898c5: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12501"/><div sID="gen22979" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12501"/>16. (Compare <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.18-Ezek.38.22">Eze 38:18-22</reference>). The victories of the Jews over their cruel foe Antiochus, under the Maccabees, may be a reference of this prophecy; but the ultimate reference is to the last Antichrist, of whom Antiochus was the type. Jerusalem being the central seat of the theocracy (<reference osisRef="Ps.132.13">Psa 132:13</reference>), it is from thence that Jehovah discomfits the foe.<div eID="gen22979" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22980" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">roar--</hi>as a lion (<reference osisRef="Jer.25.30">Jr 25:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.2">Am 1:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.3.8">3:8</reference>). Compare as to Jehovah's voice thundering, <reference osisRef="Ps.18.13">Psa 18:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.3.10">Ha 3:10</reference>, <reference osisRef="Hab.3.11">11</reference>.<div eID="gen22980" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22981" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Lord ... the hope of his people--</hi>or, "their refuge" (<reference osisRef="Ps.46.1">Psa 46:1</reference>). <div eID="gen22981" type="x-p"/>
entries.20867b42dacb1be58986c47801b5fe7b073b25ba: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12502"/><div sID="gen22982" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12502"/><hi type="bold">17. shall ye know--</hi>experimentally by the proofs of favors which I shall vouchsafe to you. So "know" (<reference osisRef="Isa.60.16">Is 60:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.20">Ho 2:20</reference>).<div eID="gen22982" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22983" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dwelling in Zion--</hi>as peculiarly your God.<div eID="gen22983" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22984" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">holy ... no strangers pass through--</hi>to attack, or to defile, the holy city (<reference osisRef="Isa.35.8">Is 35:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.1">52:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.14.21">Zec 14:21</reference>). Strangers, or Gentiles, shall come to Jerusalem, but it shall be in order to worship Jehovah there (<reference osisRef="Zech.14.16">Zec 14:16</reference>). <div eID="gen22984" type="x-p"/>
entries.750c376a101522b07bc6e837ff3fc2a59771fbb6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12503"/><div sID="gen22985" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12503"/><hi type="bold">18. mountains ... drop ... wine--</hi>figurative for abundance of vines, which were cultivated in terraces of earth between the rocks on the sides of the hills of Palestine (<reference osisRef="Amos.9.13">Am 9:13</reference>).<div eID="gen22985" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22986" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hills ... flow with milk--</hi>that is, they shall abound in flocks and herds yielding milk plentifully, through the richness of the pastures.<div eID="gen22986" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22987" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">waters--</hi>the great desideratum for fertility in the parched East (<reference osisRef="Isa.30.25">Is 30:25</reference>).<div eID="gen22987" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22988" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fountain ... of ... house of ... Lord ... water ... valley of Shittim--</hi>The blessings, temporal and spiritual, issuing from Jehovah's house at Jerusalem, shall extend even to Shittim, on the border between Moab and Israel, beyond Jordan (<reference osisRef="Num.25.1">Nu 25:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Num.33.49">33:49</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.2.1">Jos 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.6.5">Mi 6:5</reference>). "Shittim" means "acacias," which grow only in arid regions: implying that even the arid desert shall be fertilized by the blessing from Jerusalem. So <reference osisRef="Ezek.47.1-Ezek.47.12">Eze 47:1-12</reference> describes the waters issuing from the threshold of the house as flowing into the Dead Sea, and purifying it. Also in <reference osisRef="Zech.14.8">Zec 14:8</reference> the waters flow on one side into the Mediterranean, on the other side into the Dead Sea, near which latter Shittim was situated (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.46.4">Psa 46:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.1">Re 22:1</reference>). <div eID="gen22988" type="x-p"/>
entries.41705ca46a978f005743dd552d325b47590b81a2: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12504"/><div sID="gen22989" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12504"/><hi type="bold">19. Edom--</hi>It was subjugated by David, but revolted under Jehoram (<reference osisRef="2Chr.21.8-2Chr.21.10">2Ch 21:8-10</reference>); and at every subsequent opportunity tried to injure Judah. Egypt under Shishak spoiled Jerusalem under Rehoboam of the treasures of the temple and the king's house; subsequently to the captivity, it inflicted under the Ptolemies various injuries on Judea. Antiochus spoiled Egypt (<reference osisRef="Dan.11.40-Dan.11.43">Da 11:40-43</reference>). Edom was made "desolate" under the Maccabees [Josephus, Antiquities, 12.11,12]. The low condition of the two countries for centuries proves the truth of the prediction (compare <reference osisRef="Isa.19.1">Is 19:1</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Jer.49.17">Jr 49:17</reference>; Ob 10). So shall fare all the foes of Israel, typified by these two (<reference osisRef="Isa.63.1">Is 63:1</reference>, &c.). <div eID="gen22989" type="x-p"/>
entries.7e78fdbfee0ac6d7f25c8319108a5c3cd8cb5087: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12505"/><div sID="gen22990" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12505"/><hi type="bold">20. dwell for ever--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Amos.9.15">Am 9:15</reference>), that is, be established as a flourishing state. <div eID="gen22990" type="x-p"/>
entries.2d30a4a892bd1654ef3d915621f7574e9dc5bde6: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12506"/><div sID="gen22991" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12506"/><hi type="bold">21. cleanse ... blood ... not cleansed--</hi>I will purge away from Judah the extreme guilt (represented by "blood," the shedding of which was the climax of her sin, <reference osisRef="Isa.1.15">Is 1:15</reference>) which was for long not purged away, but visited with judgments (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.4">Is 4:4</reference>). Messiah saves from guilt, in order to save from punishment (<reference osisRef="Matt.1.21">Mt 1:21</reference>). <chapter eID="Joel.3"/><div eID="gen22991" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen22821" osisID="Joel" type="book"/>

entries.40877916e2cd30318e5f6dc8be084a44e80bd534: <div eID="gen34135" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen34136" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34137" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34137" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen34136" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen34138" type="x-p"/> The prophecy in this chapter is thought by some to relate to the latter times of the world, when God shall finally deliver his people from all their adversaries; and it must be confessed that the figures employed are so lofty as to render it impossible to restrain the whole of their import to any events prior to the commencement of the Christian era. The whole prophecy is delivered in a very beautiful strain of poetry; by what particular events are referred to is at present very uncertain, vv. 1-21.
entries.ea84c3ea3d0a0c6a6ca8704213035889859e46b6: <hi type="bold">Verse 2</hi> <div eID="gen34181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34182" type="x-p"/> The valley of Jehoshaphat - There is no such valley in the land of Judea; and hence the word must be symbolical. It signifies the judgment of God, or Jehovah judgeth; and may mean some place (as Bp. Newcome imagines) where Nebuchadnezzar should gain a great battle, which would utterly discomfit the ancient enemies of the Jews, and resemble the victory which Jehoshaphat gained over the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites, <reference osisRef="2Chr.20.22-2Chr.20.26">2Chr 20:22-26</reference>. <div eID="gen34182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34183" type="x-p"/> And parted my land - The above nations had frequently entered into the territories of Israel; and divided among themselves the lands they had thus overrun. <div eID="gen34183" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34184" type="x-p"/> While the Jews were in captivity, much of the land of Israel was seized on, and occupied by the Philistines, and other nations that bordered on Judea.
entries.da0121cc8d365c2414bd58d9e278e0b67432ef13: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen34184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34185" type="x-p"/> Have given a boy for a harlot - To such wretched circumstances were the poor Jews reduced in their captivity, that their children were sold by their oppressors; and both males and females used for the basest purposes. And they were often bartered for the necessaries or luxuries of life. Or this may refer to the issue of the Chaldean war in Judea, where the captives were divided among the victors. And being set in companies, they cast lots for them: and those to whom they fell sold them for various purposes; the boys to be slaves and catamites, the girls to be prostitutes; and in return for them they got wine and such things. I think this is the meaning of the text.
entries.749856c83032d3a942a7a8e9fb4a488506ae1527: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen34185" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34186" type="x-p"/> What have ye to do with me - Why have the Syrians and Sidonians joined their other enemies to oppress my people? for they who touch my people touch me. <div eID="gen34186" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34187" type="x-p"/> Will ye render me a recompense? - Do you think by this to avenge yourselves upon the Almighty? to retaliate upon God! Proceed, and speedily will I return your recompense; I will retaliate.
entries.5192cad0b405e89f320818a87e2ab16c57387885: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen34187" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34188" type="x-p"/> Ye have taken my silver and my gold - The Chaldeans had spoiled the temple, and carried away the sacred vessels, and put them in the temple of their own god in Babylon.  <chapter eID="Joel.3"/> <div eID="gen34188" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen34027" osisID="Joel" type="book"/>
entries.734a3de1496351dc974ddf3c55a05c76566d1410: <hi type="bold">Verse 6</hi> <div eID="gen34138" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34139" type="x-p"/> Sold unto the Grecians - These were the descendants of Javan, <reference osisRef="Gen.10.2-Gen.10.5">Gen 10:2-5</reference>. And with them the Tyrians trafficked, <reference osisRef="Eze.27.19">Eze 27:19</reference>. <div eID="gen34139" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34140" type="x-p"/> That ye might remove them far from their border - Intending to send them as far off as possible, that it might be impossible for them to get back to reclaim the land of which you had dispossessed them.
entries.f5d7e59458b0f7b82f9dcfeec56d8ba3aace0f19: <hi type="bold">Verse 7</hi> <div eID="gen34140" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34141" type="x-p"/> I will raise them - I shall find means to bring them back from the place whither ye have sold them, and they shall retaliate upon you the injuries they have sustained. It is said that Alexander and his successors set at liberty many Jews that had been sold into Greece. And it is likely that many returned from different lands, on the publication of the edict of Cyrus. - Newcome.
entries.cefedb4f2abc3fcb9ee61d9207d93ec2fbc491a9: <hi type="bold">Verse 8</hi> <div eID="gen34141" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34142" type="x-p"/> I will sell your sons - When Alexander took Tyre, he reduced into slavery all the lower people, and the women. Arrian, lib. ii., says that thirty thousand of them were sold. Artaxerxes Ochus destroyed Sidon, and subdued the other cities of Phoenicia. In all these wars, says Calmet, the Jews, who obeyed the Persians, did not neglect to purchase Phoenician slaves, whom they sold again to the Sabeans, or Arabs.
entries.b8376740aacab6bf454272a91ad47d9271cfaac2: <hi type="bold">Verse 9</hi> <div eID="gen34142" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34143" type="x-p"/> Prepare war - Let all the enemies of God and of his people join together; let them even call all the tillers of the ground to their assistance, instead of laboring in the field; let every peasant become a soldier. Let them turn their agricultural implements into offensive weapons, so that the weak, being well armed, may confidently say, I am strong: yet, when thus collected and armed, Jehovah will bring down thy mighty ones; for so the clause in <reference osisRef="Joe.3.11">Joe 3:11</reference> should be rendered.
entries.ebd20de7ae4114a4eebb8a7a934d0f8d1c03f1d6: <hi type="bold">Verse 12</hi> <div eID="gen34143" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34144" type="x-p"/> Let the heathen be wakened - The heathen shall be wakened. <div eID="gen34144" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34145" type="x-p"/> The valley of Jehoshaphat - Any place where God may choose to display his judgments against his enemies.
entries.7334708d40565a694251c7cff2236f2bffa2fc86: <hi type="bold">Verse 13</hi> <div eID="gen34145" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34146" type="x-p"/> Put ye in the sickle - The destruction of his enemies is represented here under the metaphor of reaping down the harvest; and of gathering the grapes, and treading them in the wine-presses.
entries.8505583715281e3ab6d87b9de6b38f105b79a663: <hi type="bold">Verse 14</hi> <div eID="gen34146" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34147" type="x-p"/> Multitudes, multitudes - המנים המנים hamonim, hamonim, crowds upon crowds, in the valley of decision, or excision: the same as the valley of Jehoshaphat, the place where God is to execute judgment on his enemies.
entries.f43d36362af509b2e83773ec195bc9f6a284717f: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen34147" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34148" type="x-p"/> The sun and the moon shall be darkened - High and mighty states shall be eclipsed, and brought to ruin, and the stars - petty states, princes, and governors - shall withdraw their shining; withhold their influence and tribute from the kingdoms to which they have belonged, and set up themselves as independent governors.
entries.612cc029b00b81b985dc0d0d9a036ba146353220: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen34148" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34149" type="x-p"/> The Lord also shall roar out of Zion - His temple and worship shall be reestablished there, and he will thence denounce his judgments against the nations. "The heavens and the earth shall shake." There shall be great commotions in powerful empires and their dependencies; but in all these things his own people shall be unmoved, for God shall be their hope and strength.
entries.29bad1c310423a300d36d2a0cde61b5156c45686: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen34149" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34150" type="x-p"/> So shall ye know - By the judgments I execute on your enemies, and the support I give to yourselves, that I am the all-conquering Jehovah; and that I have again taken up my residence in Jerusalem. All this may refer, ultimately, to the restoration of the Jews to their own land; when holiness to the Lord shall be their motto; and no strange god, or impure people, shall be permitted to enter the city, or even pass through it; they shall have neither civil nor religious connections with any who do not worship the true God in spirit and in truth. This, I think, must refer to Gospel times. It is a promise not ye fulfilled.
entries.a3c72ec9381f3be262ef987d276b36b243dd2194: <hi type="bold">Verse 18</hi> <div eID="gen34150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34151" type="x-p"/> In that day - After their return from their captivities. <div eID="gen34151" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34152" type="x-p"/> The mountains shall drop down new wine - A poetic expression for great fertility. Happy times: peace and plenty. The vines shall grow luxuriantly on the sides of the mountains; and the hills shall produce such rich pastures that the flocks shall yield abundance of milk. <div eID="gen34152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34153" type="x-p"/> And all the rivers of Judah - Far from being generally dry in the summer, shall have their channels always full of water. <div eID="gen34153" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen34154" type="x-p"/> And a fountain shall come forth of the house of the Lord - See the account of the typical waters in Ezekiel 47, to which this seems to have a reference; at least the subject is the same, and seems to point out the grace of the Gospel, the waters of salvation, that shall flow from Jerusalem, and water the valley of Shittim.
